gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 concerns unestablished regularity and perturbed-system hypotheses for applying the energy estimate, whereas the gold issue concerns an incorrect nonlinear interpolation formula and the resulting failure for nonzero-mean errors. The shared energy-estimate context does not establish recognition of the specific algebraic defect.
Both entries identify that point-sampling an L2 equivalence class at circumcenters is not well defined and propose cell-average initialization as the specific repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The FV-FE initialization uses point values although the allowed initial data are only L2 equivalence classes, so the algorithm is not canonically defined; cell averages repair this.

component_coverage.gold_component: Point-sampling the L2 initial datum at circumcenters is representative-dependent and makes initialization not well defined.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 explicitly states that L2 functions have no well-defined point values and that changing them on the sampled null set changes the algorithm output.

component_coverage.gold_component: Replacing point samples by cell averages yields a well-defined initialization on L2 equivalence classes.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 supplies the same specific cell-average repair and states that the subsequent analysis is unaffected.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-004 identifies a sign error in a residual bound. The gold issue instead concerns an underdetermined vector elliptic problem whose boundary data do not select the actual gradient, so the two defects have no substantive mathematical identity.

ISSUE-005 notes that experiments use mixed boundary conditions without extending the scheme and residual analysis, but does not identify the gold defect that existence and weak-solution results are proved only for smooth-boundary domains while main_thm claims polygonal domains, nor does it repair that existence theory.

ISSUE-001 concerns missing regularity and perturbed-system hypotheses for an energy estimate. It does not identify the circular use of stability results that already assume existence through T, which is the distinct failure in the gold issue.
